summary.headline: GKSL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 195% YoY to INR38.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 26.8%, and H1 revenue reached 88% of FY26's full-year total.
summary.overview: Gujarat Kidney and Super Speciality Ltd reported its first quarter as a listed company, with Q2 FY27 revenue of INR38.1 crore (up 11% QoQ, 195% YoY) and EBITDA of INR10.2 crore at a 26.8% margin. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR72.4 crore (up 157% YoY) and PAT was INR11.9 crore (up 44%), with growth driven largely by recently acquired hospitals and the Dubai polyclinic. Management said margins are dipping due to consolidation of acquisitions being upgraded, higher employee cost from the Dubai acquisition, and receivables built up before April 2026. Management declined to give numerical FY27 revenue or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +22% QoQ; margin up from 24.4% in Q1
+104% YoY from INR40.2 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: ~INR27 crore / ~INR17 crore; EBITDA margin 32.8%, PAT margin 20.05%

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / cash and borrowings (30 Sep 2026)
financial_highlights.value: INR263.6 crore net worth; cash INR32.2 crore vs borrowings INR17.3 crore (net cash)

segments.name: Gujarat Kidney Hospital (flagship, Vadodara)
segments.commentary: Core renal science and urology; capabilities include endourology, urologic oncology, pediatric and reconstructive urology, renal transplant and laparoscopic urology. Company has expanded into cardiology, oncology, orthopedics, OB-GYN and general surgery.

segments.name: Dubai polyclinic (Blue Tree / Globally Hospital, 51% stake)
segments.commentary: Existing revenue base of about INR20 crore; management says it has been profitable for five years. Valuation for the remaining stake has reportedly been agreed, with a buyout to be considered after one or two quarters of results. Employee cost is higher here, which management cited for margin pressure.

segments.name: Other 51%-owned subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Raj Farm in Bharuch and Patel Multispecialty in Ankleshwar are also 51%-owned and are on the list for stake-increase negotiations.

segments.name: Dialysis and pharmacy
segments.commentary: Management said dialysis margins are low relative to super-specialty surgery. Operates 10 pharmacies across the network; the number of pharmacies is given as 10.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 revenue or EBITDA margin guidance; management pointed to historical quarterly results instead.
Management said quarterly margins will fluctuate (Q1 high, Q2 lower, Q3 variable) but the full-year average will settle near the current level.
Two greenfield expansions planned: Ahmedabad hospital and Baruch hospital.
Priorities: upgrade existing hospitals, selective inorganic acquisitions, and capturing a larger share of the patient journey (OPD, diagnostics, IPD/ICU, surgery, pharmacy, follow-up).
capex_capacity: H1 FY27: about INR16.7 crore deployed on acquisitions and INR6.2 crore on capex; operating cash flow turned positive.
FY26 average bed occupancy about 65%, implying headroom within the existing capacity; average revenue per occupied bed about INR9,221 per day (consolidated).
Acquisition criteria: at least 15 years of operating history, doctor-run, clean litigation record, and a 7-year commitment from the doctors.
Network of 11 hospitals and 10 pharmacies across 9 cities.
demand_pricing: Management said ARPOB is lower on a consolidated basis because of acquired hospitals; standalone ARPOB is described as comparatively better, and a strategic plan is under internal review.
Government scheme patients are about 2% of volume; margins are under pressure from government schemes, and insurance/TPA referrals carry discounts under policy.
Direct (self-pay) case mix is the stated lever for margin expansion, with doctor compensation moved toward full-time doctors.
Receivables from before 1 April 2026 are being recovered; management said credit is now capped at roughly 102 to 115 days.

qa_highlights.question: What plans exist to lift ARPOB, and what margin trajectory and basis-point guidance can be given for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated ARPOB of about INR9,221 is dragged by acquisitions, with standalone better; it has an internal committee for a strategic plan. It gave no basis-point guidance, citing case mix, expenses, full-time doctors, and leakage control via an internal auditor.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and acquisition strategy is planned for H2, and will the company expand beyond Gujarat?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is to raise stakes in the three 51%-owned subsidiaries (Dubai, Bharuch, Ankleshwar), starting with Dubai after one or two more quarters of results. Acquisitions in or outside Gujarat are preferred over greenfield, with greenfield expansion at Ahmedabad and Baruch.

qa_highlights.question: Given the high H1 base, what full-year revenue and margin guidance can be provided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers and pointed to the quarterly history.

qa_highlights.question: Will ALOS and ARPOB rise with complex therapies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins improve with super-specialty surgery (uro, nephro-uro, cardiac) versus dialysis, and that quarterly revenue and profit are seasonal, averaging out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables are high (INR40–42 crore cited). Are customers paying or are insurers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are mainly older accumulated balances, that tight controls have applied since 1 April, and that government and insurer payments are delayed by query processes but are coming through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the Dubai Blue Tree acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blue Tree is a polyclinic run by a well-known doctor with about five years of profitability, serving as a base for medical tourism and referrals into India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow reach only about INR0.4 crore in H1 against PAT of INR11.9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The management deferred to its CA consultant and noted that acquisitions were made in the period, without giving a number or breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 48% in H1 FY26 to about 25% in FY27, and is 26% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins fluctuate and average out over time, with the current dip linked to recent acquisitions being upgraded. It gave no figure for the steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 employee cost the new run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed higher employee cost mainly to the Dubai Blue Tree acquisition, where staff costs are higher, and said the company is working to control employee cost.

risks_watch: Margin dilution from acquisitions under upgrade; management gave no steady-state margin figure, and the EBITDA margin has dropped from about 48% in H1 FY26 to about 25% in H1 FY27.
Receivables of roughly INR40–42 crore (as cited in the call) and dependence on delayed government and insurer payments; management did not confirm the balance.
Operating cash flow of about INR0.4 crore in H1 against PAT of INR11.9 crore; the reason was not quantified.
Low ARPOB on a consolidated basis and rising government-scheme exposure.

Governance and disclosure: management declined to give FY27 revenue or margin guidance and acquisition details, and the transcript has a company-name inconsistency (Chemicals/Specialty) and a reference to a 'Nazir' CA not on the management list.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the growth trajectory and balance sheet, but guarded on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 revenue, margin or acquisition specifics, and deflected several questions to historical results.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is expanding into cardiology, oncology, orthopedics, OB-GYN and general surgery, and is reviewing a strategic plan for standalone ARPOB, but no specific new product launch or date was given.

rows.label: Dubai stake buyout and medical tourism base

rows.label: Credit control and receivables recovery
rows.why: Credit is now capped at roughly 102-115 days and pre-April 2026 receivables are being recovered, though the call cited INR40-42 crore of receivables without management confirming the balance.

rows.label: Shift to self-pay and full-time doctor mix
rows.why: Direct self-pay case mix is the stated margin lever, with government scheme patients at about 2% of volume and insurer/TPA referrals discounted, but no target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth and the net-cash balance sheet (net worth INR263.6 crore, cash INR32.2 crore vs borrowings INR17.3 crore) but declined FY27 revenue and margin guidance and gave no steady-state margin figure, while analysts pressed on margin dilution, ARPOB, receivables and weak H1
